playbook:
When the escort stage comes up every round, I always name a boat — never "none." A mutual escort pays 5 points, dwarfing anything else in the game, and naming none guarantees zero. Default to naming the same live boat every round to build reciprocity.

When I pick an escort partner, I lock in exactly one boat and signal it explicitly by name in my note EVERY round from round 1 onward — in my last episode I signaled intermittently and only clearly committed at the final round, and never got the mutual. A lukewarm signal gets ignored; a relentless one gives the partner the best possible reason to believe I'll name them.

When my chosen partner has failed to reciprocate for two consecutive rounds, I switch to the other live boat and announce the switch clearly ("Foxtrot didn't respond over two rounds — Gamma, this offer moves to you now"). I do not keep naming a non-responder into the final round out of sunk cost, but I also do not flip-flop every round, which makes me look uncommitted.

When I post a note, I use it only for coordination: who I escort, who they should name back, and any retaliation observations. I never waste it on flavor like "steady on station" — notes are the only channel to set up my biggest scoring lever.

When the claim stage comes up, I always report truthfully — the rules say the claim must match my private result, and false claims risk detection and burned trust I need for escort coordination.

When I fire, I follow the standing order (my assigned next station) unless the points math says otherwise. I only fire on Harbor if I'm near zero and out of time with nothing left to lose — the 3-point transfer is small next to a mutual escort's 5, and Harbor's threat means removal, which also destroys my escort income. Early on it's never worth it.

When I choose a fire cell, I do not repeat the same cell round after round — last episode I fired 5 six times with all misses. I sweep across the sea in a non-obvious order (e.g., 2, 7, 4, 8, 3, 6), and if the public logs reveal the target's favored hide cells I bias toward those. Centrally favored hiders get caught by the middle of my sweep; pattern reveals override the sweep.

When I hide, I avoid my previous cells and any repetition, rotating among extremes (1, 2, 8, 9) since opponents likely reason the same way I do about central cells. Hiding has proven low-stakes (shots often miss), but free safety is still worth it.

When I've been hit multiple rounds by the same opponent, I note it publicly — it costs nothing and may shift their behavior.

When it's the final round and no mutual escort has formed, I still name a boat and state the exact bargain in my note ("Echo names Foxtrot right now — if you name Echo we each get 5")— a clear last-round offer can land even if earlier rounds didn't.

Standing rule: pick one escort partner early, announce it by name every round, switch only after two straight no-shows, report claims truthfully, sweep fire cells instead of repeating, hide unpredictably at the extremes, never fire on Harbor unless desperate, and spend every note on explicit coordination.

1.text:
- When the scoreboard shows me behind, I stop both-sides-loss exchanges and look for a better source of points — shooting only earns me 4 but my cycle opponent earns the same off me, so pure gunnery politics never closes a gap; escort pairs (5 each) do.
- When I choose an escort claim, I always name a boat and never "none" — mutual escort is the biggest point source in the game and "none" can never score. I use my station note each round to propose a specific pairing ("Foxtrot names Gamma — Gamma name me back") with one boat.
- Before I submit any name (escort claim or target), I check it against the actual roster from the episode header — my final-round claim went to a boat that didn't exist, which threw away a free scoring chance and made my last note a lie. Default if unsure: name the boat I most recently proposed a pairing with.
- If a proposed partner hasn't reciprocated after 2 rounds, I switch the offer to the other boat — repeating an offer nobody takes is not credibility, it's stalemate. I'll name whichever of the two partners seems more responsive in their notes.
- When a rival publicly proposes mutual escort, I name them back immediately and keep doing it every round they reciprocate.
- When everyone (including me) posts generic notes like "steady on station," nobody is coordinating — I cannot assume my pairing landed just because I named someone. I keep escorting optimistically but treat it as unearned until I see a reciprocal name.
- When I pick a hide cell, I ignore opponents' notes like "I'm at 7" — notes commit to nothing. I track only observed behavior: which cells my designated shooter has actually fired, and I hide away from those, not in them. I vary my hide every round within a small set of cells my shooter has never hit, since repeating a cell that got me hit is how I bled points.
- When I fire, I treat target choice as fixed by standing order — I always fire at my assigned station, never at Harbor (its retaliation threat plus jettison rules make the 3-point grab a trap, and I lose standing with whoever survives to shoot me later). I spend my reasoning on the cell, not the target.
- When I pick a fire cell, I don't default to the middle forever — my targets also reasoned "hiders favor mid cells" and everything missed all game. If my mid-cell shots miss repeatedly, I widen the spread (try 2–3 and 7–8), since opponents hiding "unpredictably away from the obvious" often end up near the edges. I track each miss and avoid refiring the same cell blindly.
- When I file a hit/miss claim, I always report the office's result truthfully — the claim must match the private result, so there is nothing to gain by deviating.
- When I post a note, I make it short, consistent, and transactional: one standing coordination offer (escort pairing, or a no-fire truce with the boat that shoots me in exchange for my escort), repeated each round until answered, then switched to a new partner.
- When trailing late with a couple of rounds left, I send one explicit deal note to my shooter ("stop hitting me and I'll escort you every remaining round") — a mutual escort stream (5/round) beats the 4/−1 shooting exchange for both of us, which makes the deal rational for them.
- On the final round my note and my escort claim must match the same real boat — a last-round offer to one partner followed by naming a different (or nonexistent) boat burns the only remaining chance at 5 points.
- When scores are roughly level, I keep it simple: hide unpredictably, fire at a rotating spread of plausible cells, claim truthfully, and push one escort pairing until it lands or I switch partners.

2.text:
When the board is 9 cells and I have no information, I hide near the edges (1–2, 8–9), not the salient center, and I fire close to the center (4–6) because unsophisticated opponents tend to hide there.

When I fire, I vary the cell slightly round to round around my best estimate of the opponent's hiding habit, rather than repeating the exact same cell, so an opponent tracking my shots can't simply avoid that cell.

When firing at the same target over multiple rounds and missing, I track which cells I've already fired and don't let the misses cluster in one spot: after a few central misses I sweep — center, then cells just off it, then edges — since a stubborn edge-hider will beat a pure center strategy every round, which is exactly what happened to me across six misses on Echo.

When choosing my hide, I look at who fires at me under the standing order and move off any cell I've repeated; I never sit in the cell the player targeting me has been aiming at or drifting toward.

I always claim the true result the office gives me — claims must match it — and I spend no reasoning effort on the claim stage at all.

Escort claims are the biggest source of free points and I lost them all through form errors: I filed "Alpha" and "Beta", which are not boats in the game. I only ever submit exact player names from the scoreboard (e.g. Echo, Foxtrot). Invalid names score nothing and this mistake alone forfeits up to 10+ points.

In the note stage I explicitly propose a mutual escort pact with one named boat ("I file you, you file me"), then I file that exact boat name at the escort stage, every round, consistently, so they can learn to reciprocate. Filing "none" or a garbled name leaves guaranteed points on the table.

If my pact partner does not reciprocate after two rounds (visible from my score not climbing), I switch: at the next note stage I address both other boats ("I will escort whoever escorts me, name yourself in your note") and file the one that responds. Purely one-sided pacts score zero.

I never fire at Harbor. The +3 jettison bounty is not worth being put off the board for the rest of the patrol; I always fire my standing-order target.

I keep my note short and use it only as the coordination channel: it is the one public broadcast per round, so it carries my escort proposal and nothing else.

I track the scoreboard at every hide and fire stage: if I'm ahead late, I prioritize evading whoever targets me over maximizing my own shot; if I'm behind late, I assume the opponent pattern (all misses so far) means edge-hiding and swing my fire out to cells 1–2 and 8–9 for the last rounds rather than grinding center shots that have never landed.

Final-round rule: claims and notes still follow the same discipline — truthful claims, valid names — because a final escort match (5 points) is worth more than any single shot is likely to earn.
